title: Lift two nested foam end-caps out of a carton, fit both onto a steel roller on the bench, and lower it suspended
instruction: Take both blue foam end-caps out of the shipping carton, fit one onto each end of the steel roller on the bench, and lower the roller with both end-caps together into the carton so the roller rests suspended off the floor.
context: Hand packers and packagers (O*NET 53-7064.00, 555,500 US workers) and hand laborers and material movers (O*NET 53-7062.00, 2.94 million) regularly assemble, line, and pad cartons with die-cut PE foam end-caps to isolate journals and suspend rollers and drums off the box floor. Pre-assembled shipper kits arrive at the pack bench with both 46 mm end-caps nested inside the empty 254 mm carton, leaving 162 mm between them so the 200 mm roller cannot enter; removing only one cap and plugging the roller into the other leaves 29 mm to the far wall (16 mm past the 8 mm spindle), blocking the 46 mm second cap. Each 45 mm slip-on socket has 2.5 mm/side clearance around the 40 mm steel roller with no latch, so lifting by one cap alone tips the roller out of the unheld cap under gravity; after taking both caps out and fitting them onto the roller on the bench, lowering the 250 mm unit into the carton is easiest with both hands squeezing the caps inward so the roller hangs 16 mm off the floor.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left, z up from the bench; fixed layout (object_jitter = 0, nothing varies by seed). An open-top shipping carton (ULINE 10 x 6 x 3 in Corrugated Box, SKU S-4600, 200 lb. test C-flute kraft board, inside 25.4 cm along y by 15.24 cm along x by 7.62 cm wall height, 4.0 mm wall, rim at z = 8.02 cm) has its top flaps trimmed flush at the crease and is taped square on the bench centred at (36.0, 0.0) cm (within 2 mm and 2 degrees). In front of it at (22.2, 0.0) cm, a dark-stained birch roller cradle (our fixture: 5.6 x 10.0 x 1.4 cm base with two 0.8 x 10.0 x 0.85 cm rails 2.4 cm apart inside, top z = 2.25 cm) is taped square to the bench. Resting along y on the cradle is an Interroll Series 1700 galvanised steel conveyor roller (Mfr. RD-17W1JF4EAB RL200, RS 761-3149: 4.0 cm diameter x 20.0 cm steel tube, 8.0 mm round spring-loaded steel spindle 22.6 cm overall protruding 1.3 cm per end, 400 g), its axis at z = 3.85 cm with 5.0 cm of bare tube overhanging each side of the cradle. Two blue closed-cell polyethylene foam end-caps (cut from Foam Factory Polyethylene Foam - Blue, 1.7 lb/ft3 = 27.2 kg/m3, 2 x 48 x 108 in laminated plank, 6.3 g true foam mass each; simulated at a 23.3 g mass stand-in, or a 23.3 g blue 3D-printed PLA shell) measure 4.6 cm along y by 7.4 cm tall, with a 10.4 cm-wide, 2.0 cm-tall lower base stepping to a 7.2 cm-wide upper socket block (leaving 4.02 cm finger room per side to the front and back carton walls), a 2.1 cm-deep, 4.5 cm octagonal socket centred at z = 3.85 cm, and a coaxial 2.0 x 2.0 x 1.5 cm spindle relief pocket behind the shoulder (1.0 cm solid outer wall). Both caps start pre-kitted upright on the carton floor at (36.0, +10.2) cm and (36.0, -10.2) cm, sockets facing y = 0, within 2 mm of pencil ticks 2 mm inside the end walls (checked against the ticks and start photo).
scoring: 0.0 for good if at any step the roller or either end-cap falls off the bench (z < -1.0 cm; checked from the trial video). Also checked from the trial video: both end-caps must be lifted completely clear of the carton's walls/rim at the same time (held 0.2 s = 4 steps in simulation); without that, the score is 0.0. Otherwise read at the end of the trial. 0.25: both end-caps extracted clear of the carton at least once, not currently coupled on both roller ends. 0.5: both end-caps extracted and currently fitted coaxially onto opposite ends of the roller (each 200.0 mm tube end at least 12.0 mm inside its 21.0 mm socket, radial offset at most 6.0 mm, axis angle at most 10.0 degrees), not yet suspended in the carton. 1.0: both end-caps extracted and seated upright on the carton floor within the walls (tilt at most 6.0 degrees, underside within 4.0 mm of the floor, top at most 82.2 mm), the roller seated at least 14.0 mm inside both sockets (radial offset at most 5.0 mm, axis angle at most 10.0 degrees) and level within 5.0 degrees, the roller tube's underside suspended at least 10.0 mm clear above the carton floor (nominal 16.0 mm, 0 N roller-to-carton contact), and every part of both hands at least 30.0 mm clear of carton, roller, and end-caps, held stationary (at most 2.0 mm drift) for 1.0 s (20 steps). Bench tools: a 10.0 mm square gauge bar slid underneath the roller from front to back inside the carton without touching it, a ruler against pencil rings marked 21.0 mm from each roller end (insertion = 21.0 mm minus visible gap), a phone inclinometer on the roller and cap tops, the trial video for whole-trial extraction, hands-clear and 1.0 s stillness, and the final photo.
reset_notes: Between trials, about 30 seconds: lift the coupled assembly out of the carton by both end-caps, slide both end-caps off the roller, set the two empty end-caps upright on their pencil marks inside the carton ends at (36.0, +10.2) cm and (36.0, -10.2) cm with sockets facing inward (within 2 mm and 2 degrees), and place the roller back on the bench cradle at (22.2, 0.0) cm centred between its spindles (within 2 mm). All parts are dry, closed-cell or steel, reusable without wear or rig contamination.
fidelity: Rigid bodies and contacts in PhysX; no joints, welds, latches, or scripted forces on objects. Carton and bench cradle are fixed. Both blue PE foam end-caps are rigid blocks at a 23.3 g mass stand-in (true 1.7 lb/ft3 cap is 6.3 g; foam compression is not modeled, no rule reads cap mass) with 21 mm-deep, 45 mm slip-on sockets (2.5 mm/side clearance on the 40 mm roller, friction 0.20) and 15 mm spindle pockets. In the demo, both grippers squeeze the caps inward during carry.
